papers.title: Saracatinib is an efficacious clinical candidate for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: Saracatinib (AZD0530) was identified as a potent, selective inhibitor of ALK2/ACVR1 signaling and substantially reduced heterotopic ossification in two inducible mouse models of FOP, including after short courses of treatment. The compound also blocked activin A-induced SMAD1/5 phosphorylation in FOP patient-derived fibroblasts and was generally well tolerated in the tested mouse regimens, supporting clinical repurposing for FOP prophylaxis.
papers.why: Drug screening and two in vivo models demonstrate potent suppression of heterotopic ossification by saracatinib, including after injury.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetics of Zilurgisertib With and Without Food from Single and Multiple Ascending Dose Phase 1 Studies in Healthy Adults.
papers.summary: In healthy adults, oral zilurgisertib was generally well tolerated, rapidly absorbed, and had a pharmacokinetic profile supporting once-daily dosing without regard to food. The paper also reports preclinical inhibition of wild-type and FOP-mutant ALK2 activity and dose-dependent reduction of heterotopic ossification, while saliva pharmacokinetics strongly correlated with plasma pharmacokinetics but had greater variability; efficacy in people with FOP was not evaluated.
papers.why: The phase 1 studies characterize zilurgisertib dosing, food effects, pharmacokinetics, safety, and the use of saliva as a noninvasive drug-monitoring matrix for FOP patients.

papers.title: Potent inhibition of heterotopic ossification by nuclear retinoic acid receptor-γ agonists.
papers.summary: Selective retinoic acid receptor γ agonists strongly suppressed heterotopic ossification in mouse models, including a transgenic FOP-like model carrying constitutively active ALK2Q207D, with minimal rebound and mostly minimal adverse findings. Mechanistically, the agonists reduced Smad1/4/5 abundance and Smad1/5/8 phosphorylation, dampened BMP signaling, and persistently impaired the chondrogenic and skeletogenic potential of mesenchymal progenitor cells.
papers.why: RAR-gamma agonists prevented heterotopic ossification in mesenchymal-cell and constitutively active ALK2 mouse models directly relevant to FOP.

papers.title: A new class of small molecule inhibitor of BMP signaling.
papers.summary: The paper identifies K02288 as a selective, potent small-molecule inhibitor of ALK2/ACVR1 and BMP signaling, with activity in enzymatic assays, cultured cells, and zebrafish embryos. The work presents K02288 as a pharmacological tool and preclinical starting point, but it does not test efficacy or safety in patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.why: Reports discovery and experimental characterization of a selective small-molecule ALK2 inhibitor developed specifically to treat FOP.

papers.title: Activin-dependent signaling in fibro/adipogenic progenitors causes fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: The study identifies ACVR1(R206H)-expressing fibro/adipogenic progenitors as a major cell-of-origin of injury-induced and spontaneous heterotopic ossification in conditional FOP mouse models. Activin A is an osteogenic ligand for mutant FAPs, and systemic blockade with ActA-mAb strongly or completely suppresses heterotopic ossification in transplantation, injury-induced, and spontaneous models, but was not tested as a clinical treatment.
papers.why: This genetic FOP model identifies fibro/adipogenic progenitors as a major ossification cell source and shows complete prevention of heterotopic ossification with systemic activin-A inhibition.

papers.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: mechanisms and models of skeletal metamorphosis.
papers.summary: This review identifies heterozygous activating ACVR1 mutations, especially R206H (ALK2), as the direct cause of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and links them to ligand-independent BMP pathway activation and heterotopic endochondral ossification. It highlights the Acvr1R206H/+ chimeric knock-in mouse as a high-fidelity model and describes diagnostic sequencing, candidate flare-up biomarkers, and experimental approaches for blocking ACVR1 signaling, inflammation, or mesenchymal osteogenic differentiation.
papers.why: The review documents a high-fidelity Acvr1-mutant mouse model and multiple complementary animal models that can be reused to study FOP mechanisms and therapies.

papers.title: Induced pluripotent stem cells from patients with human fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva show increased mineralization and cartilage formation.
papers.summary: Patient-derived human induced pluripotent stem cell lines carrying the ACVR1 R206H mutation reproduced key cellular features of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, including increased chondrogenesis and a stronger propensity for mineral deposition than control iPS cells. The mineralization phenotype was blocked by the BMP-signaling inhibitor DMH1, while the mutation was insufficient to cause spontaneous mineralization in FOP dermal fibroblasts.
papers.why: The paper establishes patient-derived FOP iPSC models with abnormal chondrogenesis and mineralization and shows that the phenotype is suppressed by the BMP inhibitor DMH1.

papers.title: Structure-activity relationship of 3,5-diaryl-2-aminopyridine ALK2 inhibitors reveals unaltered binding affinity for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva causing mutants.
papers.summary: This medicinal-chemistry study found that FOP-causing ACVR1/ALK2 mutants bind a series of ATP-competitive 2-aminopyridine inhibitors similarly to wild-type ALK2, supporting inhibition of diverse FOP mutants but not mutant-selective targeting. LDN-214117 emerged as a potent, ALK2-biased, kinome-selective BMP-signaling inhibitor with low HepG2 cytotoxicity, but it was evaluated biochemically and in cells rather than tested for clinical efficacy in FOP.
papers.why: The study develops selective ALK2 inhibitors with activity against FOP-mutant receptors and identifies LDN-214117 as a preclinical candidate.

papers.title: Prevalence of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) in France: an estimate based on a record linkage of two national databases.
papers.summary: Linking the CEMARA registry and PMSI national hospital database identified 89 people with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in France and yielded an estimated prevalence of 1.36 per million inhabitants. The study also characterized age at symptom onset and diagnosis and highlighted the high false-positive rate of using PMSI diagnosis codes alone to identify FOP.
papers.why: The paper identifies and quantifies FOP cases using two existing French national resources and a reusable population-scale ascertainment method.

papers.title: Modeling human somite development and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva with induced pluripotent stem cells.
papers.summary: The study establishes chemically defined protocols for generating somite derivatives and somite-derived MSC-like cells from human iPSCs, then applies them to patient-derived FOP-iPSC models. Activin A enhances chondrogenesis specifically in FOP MSC-like cells but not sclerotome-derived chondrocytes, while R667 and rapamycin attenuate this phenotype; the model also identifies PDGFRα+/CD31− cells as an enriched population exhibiting aberrant ACVR1 signaling and enhanced chondrogenesis.
papers.why: The study provides a disease-specific human iPSC model that reproduces enhanced chondrogenesis in FOP-derived MSC-like cells and can support mechanistic studies and cell-based therapy development.

papers.title: Natural history of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: cross-sectional analysis of annotated baseline phenotypes.
papers.summary: In this prospective natural-history cohort of 114 individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, increasing age was associated with greater functional disability and a larger body burden of heterotopic ossification. Whole-body CT–measured heterotopic ossification correlated with clinician- and patient-reported functional impairment and was proposed as a potentially sensitive clinical-study endpoint, although longitudinal confirmation was not yet available.
papers.why: This large FOP natural-history study validates functional outcome measures and CT-based heterotopic-ossification burden as potentially useful clinical-trial endpoints.

papers.title: The ACVR1 R206H mutation found in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva increases human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived endothelial cell formation and collagen production through BMP-mediated SMAD1/5/8 signaling.
papers.summary: Patient-derived FOP hiPSC endothelial cells carrying endogenous ACVR1 R206H showed altered endothelial differentiation, increased fibroblastic and extracellular matrix gene expression, and greater BMP4-triggered SMAD1/5/8 signaling. They did not form mature mineral-depositing osteoblasts, supporting a fibrosis-priming and niche-support role rather than direct endothelial-to-osteoblast conversion under the tested conditions.
papers.why: The study creates an endogenous-mutation human iPSC endothelial model and identifies cell-specific BMP-SMAD responses relevant to FOP-associated fibrogenic and osteogenic phenotypes.

papers.title: BMP-dependent, injury-induced stem cell niche as a mechanism of heterotopic ossification.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study identifies a three-domain injury-induced mesenchymal stem cell niche in the Nse-BMP4 mouse model and finds the same zonal organization in acquired HO and FOP biopsy specimens. It provides experimental evidence that niche-dwelling progenitor populations and coordinated BMP and hedgehog signaling regulate heterotopic ossification, while highlighting the model, lineage-tracing, depletion, and histological methods that can accelerate mechanistic research.
papers.why: The study identifies a reproducible injury-induced MSC niche and associated lineage and signaling markers in animal lesions and patient FOP/acquired-HO biopsies.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Garetosmab (Anti-Activin A): Results From a First-in-Human Phase 1 Study.
papers.summary: In healthy nonchildbearing women, a single intravenous or subcutaneous dose of garetosmab was generally well tolerated and exhibited nonlinear, target-mediated pharmacokinetics; intravenous garetosmab increased serum total activin A in a dose-dependent manner. Preclinical findings summarized by the paper indicate that activin A inhibition prevented new heterotopic ossification and halted existing ossification in a humanized ACVR1 R206H FOP model, supporting evaluation in patients with FOP.
papers.why: The first-in-human FOP study provides direct dose, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, target-engagement, and safety data for garetosmab.

papers.title: ACVR1R206H FOP mutation alters mechanosensing and tissue stiffness during heterotopic ossification.
papers.summary: The ACVR1R206H mutation produces a locally stiff, highly organized extracellular matrix before heterotopic bone forms in an Acvr1R206H/+ mouse model of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. Mutant mesenchymal progenitor cells also misinterpret soft substrates as stiff, overactivate Rho/ROCK mechanosignaling, and increase nuclear RUNX2 localization, providing mechanistic links among enhanced BMP signaling, altered mechanobiology, and premature chondro/osteogenic differentiation.
papers.why: The study directly characterizes an ACVR1 R206H FOP mouse model and experimental assays of abnormal mechanosensing during heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Pathogenic ACVR1<sup>R206H</sup> activation by Activin A-induced receptor clustering and autophosphorylation.
papers.summary: The study shows that the common ACVR1 R206H mutation in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma causes enhanced Activin A–induced SMAD1/5 signaling by enabling ACVR1 receptor clustering and auto-activation. Genetic, inhibitor, optogenetic, and live-imaging experiments show that the mutant receptor requires ACVR2A/B structurally but, unlike wild-type ACVR1, does not predominantly require upstream ACVR1B/C kinase activity.
papers.why: The paper provides direct mechanistic data for the FOP-causing ACVR1 mutation and establishes experimentally testable receptor-activation mechanisms and assays.

papers.title: Palovarotene for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP): Results of a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Phase 2 Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized phase 2 trial found that 6 weeks of palovarotene started during an FOP flare-up produced numerical reductions in new heterotopic ossification, particularly with the 10/5-mg regimen, but the differences from placebo did not reach statistical significance. Palovarotene was generally well tolerated, although mucocutaneous adverse events and transient lipase elevations occurred, and the short duration, low enrollment, insensitive primary imaging method, and delayed treatment initiation limited efficacy assessment.
papers.why: A randomized phase 2 trial directly tested palovarotene for prevention of heterotopic ossification in FOP and reported radiologic and CT outcomes.

papers.title: Suppression of heterotopic ossification in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva using AAV gene delivery.
papers.summary: The paper develops three rAAV-based strategies for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: ACVR1 gene replacement, ACVR1R206H allele-specific silencing, and a combined amiR-RH6.ACVR1opt treatment. The combination reduced aberrant Activin A/BMP signaling and chondrogenic or osteogenic differentiation in human FOP iPSCs, and strongly suppressed traumatic and spontaneous heterotopic ossification in conditional Acvr1R206H knock-in mice.
papers.why: AAV9-based gene replacement and allele-specific silencing reduced abnormal signaling and heterotopic ossification in patient-derived cells and FOP model mice.

papers.title: Antisense-oligonucleotide mediated exon skipping in activin-receptor-like kinase 2: inhibiting the receptor that is overactive in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: The paper shows that a mouse ALK2 antisense oligonucleotide can induce exon 8 skipping, reduce full-length Alk2 expression by approximately 70–80%, and inhibit excessive BMP signaling and osteogenic differentiation in mouse myoblast, endothelial, and osteoprogenitor cells. These findings support ALK2 exon skipping as a potential FOP therapy, but no patient, animal, or clinical efficacy data are presented, and an allele-specific human ACVR1 AON was not successfully produced.
papers.why: The study demonstrates exon-skipping antisense oligonucleotides that reduce ALK2 signaling and suppress osteoblast differentiation relevant to FOP.

papers.title: Anti-ACVR1 antibodies exacerbate heterotopic ossification in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) by activating FOP-mutant ACVR1.
papers.summary: In a genetically accurate mouse model and complementary cellular systems, bivalent anti-ACVR1 antibodies dimerized FOP-mutant ACVR1, activated Smad1/5/8 signaling, exacerbated heterotopic ossification, increased hepcidin, and reduced serum iron. Monovalent anti-ACVR1 Fabs did not dimerize the receptor and instead reduced heterotopic ossification, while anti-ACVR1 antibodies inhibited wild-type ACVR1 and reduced trauma-induced ossification in non-FOP mice.
papers.why: The study experimentally shows that anti-ACVR1 antibodies activate FOP-mutant ACVR1 and worsen ossification, providing an important tested negative therapy result.

papers.title: Structural basis for the potent and selective binding of LDN-212854 to the BMP receptor kinase ALK2.
papers.summary: The study determined the crystal structure of the human ACVR1/ALK2 kinase domain in complex with LDN-212854 and showed that the inhibitor binds the ATP-binding pocket through hinge-region and water-mediated hydrogen bonds. The structure explains ALK2 selectivity and provides a template for inhibitors intended to counter gain-of-function ACVR1 variants in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.why: This study structurally validates the selective ALK2 inhibitor LDN-212854 and provides a design template for FOP drug development.

papers.title: Monitoring and Management of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva: Current Perspectives.
papers.summary: This review describes ACVR1/ALK2 gain-of-function signaling as a central mechanism of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), leading through SMAD1/5/9 activation and inflammation to heterotopic ossification. It identifies CT, 18F-NaF PET/CT, CAJIS, and cardiopulmonary testing as monitoring approaches, while describing corticosteroids and several investigational therapies whose clinical efficacy remains incompletely established.
papers.why: The review provides concrete clinical monitoring, complication-surveillance, and management approaches for tracking and reducing FOP-related morbidity.

papers.title: An anti-ACVR1 antibody exacerbates heterotopic ossification by fibro-adipogenic progenitors in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva mice.
papers.summary: In two genetically modified FOP mouse models, the bivalent anti-ACVR1 monoclonal antibody JAB0505 profoundly worsened injury-induced heterotopic ossification rather than suppressing it. Mechanistic experiments showed that JAB0505 can weakly agonize ACVR1(R206H), expand and prolong recruitment of R206H-expressing fibro-adipogenic progenitors to skeletogenic lineages, and sustain the post-injury immune response, raising safety concerns for anti-ACVR1 antibody therapy in FOP.
papers.why: Direct testing in FOP models shows that the bivalent anti-ACVR1 antibody JAB0505 has agonist activity and exacerbates heterotopic ossification, an important reusable safety finding.

papers.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva mutant ACVR1 signals by multiple modalities in the developing zebrafish.
papers.summary: In developing zebrafish embryos, FOP-associated ACVR1-R206H and ACVR1-G328R overactivate pSmad1/5 signaling through both ligand-independent and ligand-responsive mechanisms. Unlike wild-type ACVR1, the mutants do not require an intact ligand-binding domain for basal signaling or the normal type I BMP receptor partner Bmpr1, although ligand responsiveness still requires the ligand-binding domain.
papers.why: The study develops and applies a zebrafish assay demonstrating ligand-independent and ligand-responsive BMP hyperactivation by FOP ACVR1 mutants.

papers.title: Recent Advances in ALK2 Inhibitors.
papers.summary: This review identifies ACVR1/ALK2 gain-of-function signaling as a target for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and summarizes chemical series, selectivity, pharmacokinetic properties, and preclinical efficacy of ALK2 inhibitors. LDN-193189, LDN-212854, and saracatinib inhibited heterotopic ossification or bone formation in ALK2Q207D-based FOP models, while several additional inhibitors had advanced to clinical development; clinical efficacy in FOP was not yet established.
papers.why: This FOP-focused review summarizes developed selective ALK2 inhibitors and their potency, selectivity, pharmacokinetic, and in-vivo evidence for targeting the causal receptor.

papers.title: ACVR1, a therapeutic target of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, is negatively regulated by miR-148a.
papers.summary: The study shows that miR-148a directly binds the 3′ untranslated region of ACVR1 mRNA and reduces endogenous ACVR1 mRNA and protein expression in HeLa cells. Reduced ACVR1 expression was associated with suppression of BMP pathway readouts, suggesting miR-148a as a potential therapeutic target for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, although no FOP patients or patient-derived models were tested.
papers.why: Provides experimental evidence that miR-148a suppresses ACVR1 expression and BMP signaling, identifying a potential gene-regulatory therapeutic approach for FOP.

papers.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: current concepts from bench to bedside.
papers.summary: This review describes fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) as an ACVR1 gain-of-function disorder in which inflammation and dysregulated bone morphogenetic protein signaling drive mesenchymal progenitor cells toward endochondral heterotopic ossification. It identifies diagnostic DNA sequencing, several animal and cell models, and pharmacologic strategies—including palovarotene, garetosmab, and rapamycin—with supporting evidence ranging from cellular findings and clinical experience to preclinical testing, while noting major treatment limitations and unresolved mechanistic questions.
papers.why: This same-disease translational review consolidates experimental models, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and multiple BMP/ACVR1-directed agents that have reached clinical testing.

papers.title: Is fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva an interleukin-1 driven auto-inflammatory syndrome?
papers.summary: In a single 13.5-year-old patient with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, sequential anakinra and canakinumab treatment was associated with fewer and shorter flares, fewer new lumps, and smaller, softer lesions than prior anti-inflammatory treatment. Plasma IL-1β increased markedly during a flare and was undetectable during anti-IL-1 treatment, supporting an IL-1β-associated inflammatory mechanism, but the single-patient design and absence of an FOP laboratory model preclude firm causal conclusions.
papers.why: Reports reduced flare frequency and duration with anti-IL-1 therapy in one FOP patient and links elevated plasma IL-1β to disease paroxysms.

papers.title: Successful experience of tofacitinib treatment in patients with Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: In a retrospective observational cohort of 13 patients with genetically confirmed fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva who had failed standard care, tofacitinib was associated with fewer inflammatory flares, reduced corticosteroid use, improved joint motion in some patients, and favorable short-term tolerability. The evidence is limited by the small uncontrolled cohort, attrition at later time points, and absence of quantitative imaging data for new-bone volume.
papers.why: This report describes clinical use of the JAK inhibitor tofacitinib in patients with FOP, directly providing a tested therapeutic solution for inflammatory FOP flares.

papers.title: ActivinA Induced SMAD1/5 Signaling in an iPSC Derived EC Model of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) Can Be Rescued by the Drug Candidate Saracatinib.
papers.summary: The paper establishes ACVR1 R206H FOP induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived endothelial cells that reproduce the pathogenic ActivinA/SMAD1/5 response and an ActivinA-induced BMP/NOTCH transcriptional program associated with vascular development. Saracatinib suppressed aberrant SMAD1/5 phosphorylation and restored the FOP endothelial transcriptome toward wild-type levels while preserving SMAD2/3 signaling, but effects on clinical FOP were not tested.
papers.why: Establishes a human iPSC-derived FOP endothelial model and shows that saracatinib rescues abnormal Activin A/BMP-NOTCH transcriptional signaling.

papers.title: Heterotopic ossification in mice overexpressing Bmp2 in Tie2+ lineages.
papers.summary: The study establishes Tie2CRE/+;Bmp2tg/tg mice as a model of severe, spontaneously developing heterotopic ossification that resembles acquired HO and some aspects of FOP, although it does not reproduce FOP-associated congenital phenotypes. The model indicates that aberrant BMP2 activity promotes inflammation and expansion of skeletal-muscle fibro-adipogenic progenitors, while hematopoietic BMP2 expression accelerates but is neither required nor sufficient to initiate HO.
papers.why: Develops a BMP2-driven mouse model reproducing FOP-like heterotopic ossification and shows that hematopoietic-cell transplantation delays but does not prevent disease.

papers.title: Retinoid Agonists in the Targeting of Heterotopic Ossification.
papers.summary: This review describes retinoid signaling as an anti-chondrogenic mechanism and evaluates RARγ-selective agonists, particularly palovarotene, as inhibitors of heterotopic ossification in FOP. Preclinical models and post hoc clinical analyses support reduced new heterotopic bone formation, but skeletal immaturity is associated with risks including premature growth plate closure.
papers.why: This review consolidates experimental model evidence and clinical data supporting retinoid agonists, particularly palovarotene, as disease-modifying treatments for FOP.

papers.title: ACVR1 gene mutation in sporadic Korean patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: All 12 examined Korean patients with definite or clinically ambiguous fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva carried a de novo heterozygous ACVR1 c.617G>A; p.R206H point mutation. Direct sequencing and restriction-endonuclease digestion confirmed the diagnosis in ambiguous cases, supporting early genetic diagnosis before catastrophic ectopic ossification develops.
papers.why: Mutation analysis confirmed the FOP diagnosis in 12 patients with ambiguous clinical features, demonstrating its diagnostic utility in this cohort.

papers.title: Overexpression of Wild-Type ACVR1 in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva Mice Rescues Perinatal Lethality and Inhibits Heterotopic Ossification.
papers.summary: This study shows that conditional or global overexpression of wild-type human ACVR1 substantially suppresses Acvr1 R206H-associated fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva phenotypes in mice, including perinatal lethality, skeletal malformations, spontaneous heterotopic ossification, and injury-induced heterotopic ossification. The protective effect is associated with reduced activin A-induced pSMAD1/5/8 osteogenic signaling in fibro/adipogenic progenitors, although tibial exostosis was not eliminated in every model.
papers.why: The study directly tests a genetic therapeutic strategy in FOP mice and shows that ACVR1 overexpression rescues lethality and substantially suppresses heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: How Activin A Became a Therapeutic Target in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: This review identifies Activin A as a necessary and sufficient ligand for heterotopic ossification in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), acting through FOP-variant ACVR1 rather than ligand-independent receptor activity or BMP hyperresponsiveness. Activin A blockade with the investigational antibody garetosmab prevents new lesions in FOP mice and markedly reduces new lesion activity in patients, although the phase 2 primary endpoint was not statistically significant and the drug had increased mild-to-moderate adverse events.
papers.why: The abstract reports that Activin A blockade with garetosmab prevented heterotopic ossification in FOP mice and inhibited new lesions in a phase 2 FOP trial.

papers.title: AAV-Mediated Targeting of the Activin A-ACVR1R206H Signaling in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study developed an AAV9 gene therapy that silences mutant ACVR1R206H and Activin A, expresses wild-type codon-optimized ACVR1, and limits hepatic transgene expression through miR-122. In FOP mouse models and patient- or mouse-derived stromal cells, the therapy reduced aberrant BMP-Smad1/5 signaling, osteogenic differentiation, and trauma-induced heterotopic ossification, while long-term safety, immune effects, and efficacy against spontaneous HO remain unresolved.
papers.why: The study developed an AAV gene therapy that reduced trauma-induced heterotopic bone formation in ACVR1 R206H FOP mice while limiting off-target organ expression.

papers.title: Polymodal allosteric regulation of Type 1 Serine/Threonine Kinase Receptors via a conserved electrostatic lock.
papers.summary: Molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations, network analysis, and cellular reporter experiments show that the FOP-associated ALK2R206H mutation allosterically destabilizes the catalytic-site D354-R375 electrostatic lock while preserving FKBP12 binding, thereby bypassing FKBP12-mediated inhibition and producing leaky BMP signaling. Conserved disruption of this lock in ALK2, ALK3, and ALK6 supports a shared regulatory mechanism and suggests a strategy for selectively targeting disease-related mutant STKR1 receptors.
papers.why: The study provides computational and experimental evidence for a conserved allosteric ALK2 activation mechanism that supplies a direct FOP drug-targeting strategy.

papers.title: Challenges and Opportunities for Drug Repositioning in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: This review identifies aberrant ACVR1/ALK2 signalling, including neofunctional activin-A responses, BMP hypersensitivity, and downstream PI3K/AKT, mTOR, and noncanonical pathways, as central mechanisms in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. It summarizes FOP-relevant cellular and animal models and drug-repositioning evidence for saracatinib, alpelisib, rapamycin, palovarotene, imatinib, garetosmab, and other agents, while documenting null findings and toxicity concerns.
papers.why: The review consolidates tested repurposed drugs, screening models, and clinical-stage ALK2-targeted approaches that can be reused in FOP research.

papers.title: TGF-Beta Induces Activin A Production in Dermal Fibroblasts Derived from Patients with Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: In primary dermal fibroblasts from five patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, TGFβ1 selectively increased Activin A production through increased INHBA expression, whereas TNFα and IL-6 produced little or no Activin A. BMP4 increased Activin A and TGFβ1 in both FOP and control cells, and the findings nominate TGFβ1 as a possible upstream therapeutic target, but the study did not test a clinical intervention.
papers.why: Using fibroblasts from five FOP patients, the study demonstrates TGFβ1-driven Activin A production and identifies a mechanistically grounded therapeutic target for FOP heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Protocol paper: a multi-center, double-blinded, randomized, 6-month, placebo-controlled study followed by 12-month open label extension to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Saracatinib in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (STOPFOP).
papers.summary: This protocol describes the phase 2a STOPFOP trial evaluating saracatinib (AZD0530) for prevention of heterotopic ossification in adults with classic ACVR1/ALK2 R206H fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. Saracatinib is described as a low-nanomolar ALK2 inhibitor that prevented heterotopic ossification in two FOP mouse models, but this paper reports no clinical efficacy or safety results.
papers.why: The protocol reports a drug-repurposing trial and outcome-measure framework specifically designed to test saracatinib, an ACVR1/ALK2 inhibitor, in FOP.

papers.title: Oxidative phosphorylation is a pivotal therapeutic target of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: Activin A-driven FOP chondrogenesis activates mTORC1-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), with a metabolic shift from glycolysis toward OXPHOS in FOP patient-derived mesenchymal stem cells. Inhibition of mitochondrial complex I with IACS-010759 suppressed cartilage matrix formation and heterotopic ossification in vitro and in an injury-induced FOP-ACVR1 mouse model, supporting OXPHOS as a potential therapeutic target.
papers.why: The study experimentally identifies oxidative phosphorylation as a therapeutic target and shows that IACS-010759 suppresses heterotopic ossification in FOP-relevant cellular and mouse systems.

papers.title: Study methodology and insights from the palovarotene clinical development program in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: This paper reports that the palovarotene clinical development program established longitudinal outcome measures and feasible flare-up and chronic-treatment regimens for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). Natural-history and phase II data showed numerically less new heterotopic ossification with palovarotene than with placebo but no statistically significant treatment trend, while cited MOVE results showed reduced new ossification volume, with premature physeal closure identified as a safety risk in skeletally immature participants.
papers.why: The paper provides reusable FOP natural-history, imaging, dosing, and clinical-endpoint methods developed through the palovarotene development program.

papers.title: Palovarotene Action Against Heterotopic Ossification Includes a Reduction of Local Participating Activin A-Expressing Cell Populations.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of acquired heterotopic ossification, palovarotene markedly suppressed ossification and reduced the abundance of Inhba/activin A-expressing chondrogenic cells and macrophages while weakening predicted cell-cell communication. Palovarotene inhibited the chondrogenic phenotype in primary chondrocytes but did not directly reduce Inhba expression in those cells, indicating that its reduction of local activin A-producing populations is indirect or context-dependent.
papers.why: The study provides experimental evidence that palovarotene suppresses heterotopic ossification and activin A-associated HO-forming cell populations through a pathway relevant to FOP.

papers.title: Long-term use of interleukin-1 inhibitors reduce flare activity in patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: In this four-patient case series, IL-1 inhibition with anakinra or especially canakinumab was associated with substantially reduced FOP flare activity, less pain, improved patient-reported general health, and minimal formation of new heterotopic ossification sites. Withdrawal-associated recurrence and renewed suppression supported an effect, but the uncontrolled observational design, small sample, undefined optimal regimen, and incomplete objective assessment of heterotopic ossification and function limit causal and long-term conclusions.
papers.why: A four-patient case series reports that long-term IL-1 inhibition reduces FOP flare activity and new heterotopic ossification, with improvements in patient-reported pain and health outcomes.

papers.title: Suppressed prefrontal cortex oscillations associate with clinical pain in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
papers.summary: In 17 patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, resting-state functional near-infrared spectroscopy showed that moderate-to-severe pain was associated with reduced slow-5 oscillation power in the prefrontal cortex. The study also identified associations between pain and depressive or physical stress symptoms and supports fNIRS as an objective method for investigating central pain mechanisms in FOP.
papers.why: The study identifies an FOP-specific fNIRS pain-associated biomarker and supports objective monitoring of central pain mechanisms.

papers.title: Whole-body Computed Tomography Versus Dual Energy X‑ray Absorptiometry for Assessing Heterotopic Ossification in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 10 adults with classic fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, low-dose whole-body computed tomography identified more regional heterotopic ossification, produced fewer non-evaluable regions, and enabled three-dimensional volume measurement than dual energy X-ray absorptiometry. The authors selected low-dose whole-body computed tomography as the preferred modality for measuring total body heterotopic ossification burden in subsequent natural-history research.
papers.why: Direct comparison in FOP patients showed that low-dose whole-body CT is more sensitive and less ambiguous than DXA for assessing total heterotopic ossification burden.

papers.title: Functional Testing of Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP) Pathway Variants Identified on Whole-Exome Sequencing in a Patient with Delayed-Onset Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) Using ACVR1<sup>R206H</sup> -Specific Human Cellular and Zebrafish Models.
papers.summary: In an ACVR1 R206H FOP patient with delayed-onset heterotopic ossification, whole-exome sequencing identified BMPR1A R443C and ACVR2A V173I as candidate modifiers, but neither variant attenuated ACVR1 R206H signaling in functional studies. Receptor knockdown reduced ligand-stimulated pSMAD 1/5/9 signaling in human cells, and combined type I/type II receptor reduction partially rescued ventralization in zebrafish, whereas ACVR2A V173I unexpectedly increased signaling in the ACVR1 R206H zebrafish background.
papers.why: The paper develops cellular, zebrafish, molecular-modeling, and knockdown approaches for functionally testing BMP-pathway variants in FOP.

papers.title: An Open-Label Extension Study of Palovarotene Treatment in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP)
papers.summary:
Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a rare, severely disabling disease characterized by heterotopic ossification (HO), i.e., abnormal bone formation, often associated with painful, recurrent episodes of soft tissue swelling (flare-ups). Lesions begin in early childhood and lead to progressive ankyloses of major joints with resultant loss of movement.

In this study, the ability of different palovarotene dosing regimens to prevent the formation of new HO will be evaluated in adult and pediatric participants with FOP.

papers.title: Study Evaluating the Effect of Food on the Pharmacokinetics of Palovarotene and the Effect of Palovarotene on the Pharmacokinetics of the CYP3A4 Substrate Midazolam in Two Cohorts of Healthy Adult Subjects
papers.summary: Study to evaluate the effect of food and the effect of swallowing capsule whole versus sprinkling on apple sauce on the pharmacokinetics (PK)/bioavailability of palovarotene, and evaluate the effect of palovarotene on the PK of the CYP3A4 substrate midazolam.

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness and Safety of 2 Dosage Regimens of Oral Fidrisertib (IPN60130) for the Treatment of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP).
papers.summary:
Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a rare, severely disabling disease characterized by the presence of bone in soft tissue where bone normally does not exist, known as Heterotopic Ossification (HO). It is often associated with painful, recurrent episodes of soft tissue swelling (flare-ups) that lead to abnormal stiffening and immobility (ankyloses) of major joints with cumulative and irreversible loss of movement and disability.

This study will evaluate the efficacy of 2 dosing regimens of IPN60130 in inhibiting new HO volume compared with placebo (a dummy treatment) in adult and

papers.title: Study of Single-Ascending Doses of DS-6016a in Healthy Japanese Subjects
papers.summary: This study will assess the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of DS-6016a after subcutaneous injection in healthy Japanese participants.

papers.title: A Study of Andecaliximab in Participants With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP)
papers.summary:
This study is researching an experimental drug called andecaliximab. The study will include pediatric and adult patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The study will evaluate how safe and effective andecaliximab is in patients with FOP.

The study is looking at several research questions, including:

* Safety of andecaliximab in participants with FOP
* Whether andecaliximab reduces the number of new heterotopic bone lesions (Heterotopic Ossification; HO)
* Whether andecaliximab reduces the number or severity of flare-ups
* Pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD): How much

papers.title: Saracatinib Trial TO Prevent FOP
papers.summary:
This is a phase 2 study, designed as a European multicentre 6-month double blind random-ized controlled trial (RCT) of AZD0530 versus matched placebo, followed by a 12 month trial comparing open-label extended AZD0530 treatment with historical control data.

Study population: Male and female adult patients aged 18 years and older with a diagnosis of FOP who meet the inclusion (active disease) and exclusion criteria will be eligible for participation in this study. The total number of enrolled patients will be 20.

Intervention: Patients will be randomized to receive either AZD0530 100mg once d

papers.title: To Assess the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability of INCB000928 in Participants With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva
papers.summary: This Phase 2, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study is intended to evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, and Tolerability and PK of INCB000928 administered to participants with a clinical diagnosis of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

papers.title: A Rollover Study to Further Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Palovarotene Capsules in Male and Female Participants Aged ≥14 Years With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) Who Have Completed the Relevant Parent Studies.
papers.summary:
The main objective of this study is to further evaluate the safety and efficacy of palovarotene in adult and paediatric participants with FOP.

The aim of the study is also to ensure treatment continuity to participants who have completed one of the parent studies (Study PVO-1A-301, Study PVO-1A-202 and Study PVO-1A-204) and who, in the investigator's judgement, may benefit from palovarotene therapy.

papers.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Palovarotene for the Treatment of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
papers.summary: Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a rare, severely disabling disease characterized by heterotopic ossification (HO) often associated with painful, recurrent episodes of soft tissue swelling (flare-ups) that lead to ankyloses of major joints with cumulative and irreversible loss of movement and disability.

papers.title: In-Home Evaluation of Episodic Administration of Palovarotene in Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) Subjects
papers.summary: Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) is a rare, severely disabling disease characterized by painful, recurrent episodes of soft tissue swelling (flare-ups) that result in abnormal bone formation (heterotopic ossification or HO) in muscles, tendons, and ligaments. Flare-ups begin early in life and may occur spontaneously or after soft tissue trauma, vaccinations, or influenza infections. Recurrent flare-ups progressively restrict movement by locking joints leading to cumulative loss of function and disability. Mouse models of FOP have demonstrated the ability of retinoic acid receptor ga

papers.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of Palovarotene to Treat Preosseous Flare-ups in FOP Subjects
papers.summary: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is a rare, severely disabling disease characterized by painful, recurrent episodes of soft tissue swelling (flare-ups) that result in abnormal bone formation in muscles, tendons, and ligaments. Flare-ups begin early in life and may occur spontaneously or after soft tissue trauma, vaccinations, or influenza infections. Recurrent flare-ups progressively restrict movement by locking joints leading to cumulative loss of function and disability. Mouse models of FOP have demonstrated the ability of retinoic acid receptor (RAR) gamma agonists to prevent het

papers.title: A Study to Investigate the Safety, Pharmacokinetics (PK), and Efficacy of Garetosmab in Children and Adolescents With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP)
papers.summary:
This study is researching an experimental drug called garetosmab, referred to as "study drug". The study is focused on children and adolescent participants with FOP.

The aim of the study is to see how safe, tolerable, and effective the study drug is.

The study is looking at several other research questions, including:

* What side effects may happen from taking the study drug
* How much study drug is in the blood at different times
* Whether the body makes antibodies against the study drug (which could make the study drug less effective or could lead to side effects)

papers.title: A Study to Examine the Safety, Tolerability and Effects on Abnormal Bone Formation of REGN2477 in Patients With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva
papers.summary:
This is a three period study design consisting of a 6-month, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled treatment (period 1) followed by a 6-month, open-label treatment (period 2) and a follow-up treatment period (period 3).

Primary safety objective of the study is to assess the safety and tolerability of REGN2477 in male and female patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

Primary efficacy objective of the study is to assess the effect of REGN2477 versus placebo on the change from baseline in heterotopic ossification (HO) in patients with FOP, as determined by 18-NaF uptak

papers.title: A Study to Assess Safety, Tolerability and Efficacy of Garetosmab Versus Placebo Administered Intravenously (IV) in Adult Participants With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP)
papers.summary:
This study is researching an experimental drug called garetosmab. The study is focused on adult patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).

The aim of the study is to see how safe and effective the study drug is in patients with FOP.

The study is looking at several other research questions, including:

* What side effects may happen from receiving the study drug
* How much study drug is in the blood at different times
* Whether the body makes antibodies against the study drug (which could make the drug less effective or could lead to side effects)

papers.title: Study to Assess the Efficacy and Safety of Garetosmab in Japanese Adult Patients With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP)
papers.summary:
The primary safety objective of the study is to assess the safety and tolerability of garetosmab in Japanese male and female adult patients with FOP.

The primary efficacy objective of the study is to assess the effect of garetosmab on Heterotopic ossification (HO) in Japanese adult patients with FOP, as determined by the number of new heterotopic bone lesions identified by computed tomography (CT).

papers.title: Open Targets drug and clinical candidates for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva
Open Targets drugs acting on INHBA
Open Targets drugs acting on ACVR1
Targeted Therapies in Myelofibrosis: Present Landscape, Ongoing Studies, and Future Perspectives.
papers.summary: This review reports that momelotinib, a JAK1/2 inhibitor that also targets ACVR1 (ALK2), has clinically meaningful erythropoietic activity in myelofibrosis, including improved red-cell transfusion independence and anemia outcomes. Pacritinib also inhibits ACVR1 and regulates hepcidin synthesis, but the clinical benefit of its ACVR1-related mechanism is not isolated from its other activities.

papers.title: Momelotinib: Mechanism of action, clinical, and translational science.
papers.summary: This review describes momelotinib as a JAK1/JAK2 and ACVR1 inhibitor that suppresses hyperactive JAK–STAT signaling in myelofibrosis while additionally reducing hepcidin and improving iron availability, erythropoiesis, and anemia. Clinical and translational data reviewed support benefits for myelofibrosis-related anemia, transfusion burden, splenomegaly, and constitutional symptoms, but the paper does not study fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva or establish transfer to activin A–ALK2 signaling in that disease.

papers.title: Antagonizing Activin A/p15INK4b Signaling as Therapeutic Strategy for Liver Disease.
papers.summary: The paper identifies NUCC-555 as a small-molecule activin A antagonist that blocks activin A signaling in hepatocytes and hepatic stellate cells, increases early hepatocyte proliferation after partial hepatectomy, and reduces fibrosis progression in thioacetamide-treated rats and carbon tetrachloride-treated mice. These findings provide preclinical evidence that activin A signaling can be therapeutically targeted, although the experiments were performed in liver systems rather than fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.

papers.title: ACVR1 mediates renal tubular EMT in kidney fibrosis via AKT activation.
papers.summary: The paper shows that ACVR1 is induced during TGF-β1-associated renal tubular epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in HK-2 cells and a UUO mouse model. ACVR1 knockdown reduced EMT markers and AKT phosphorylation, whereas the AKT inhibitor MK2206 and AKT activator SC79 modulated α-SMA expression, supporting an ACVR1–AKT pathway in kidney fibrosis; the abstract does not explicitly study or name activin A signaling.

papers.title: Momelotinib in myelofibrosis.
papers.summary: This review reports that momelotinib is a Janus kinase inhibitor that also inhibits type 1 kinase activin A receptor/activin receptor-like kinase-2 (ACVR1/ALK2), rebalances SMAD pathways, and reduces hepcidin transcription. In myelofibrosis, clinical trials cited by the review associate momelotinib with reduced spleen size, symptom improvement, and improved anemia, although the evidence is presented as a review rather than new data from this paper.

papers.title: Emerging Therapeutic Approaches for Anemia in Myelofibrosis.
papers.summary: This review reports that activin-receptor inhibition and activin ligand traps, including momelotinib, pacritinib, luspatercept, and elritercept, are being developed to improve cytopenias and anemia in myelofibrosis. Elritercept reduced transfusion requirements in the RESTORE trial, while the anti-hemojuvelin antibody DISC-0974 decreased hepcidin, increased serum iron, and enhanced erythropoiesis.

papers.title: Uncovering Tumor-Promoting Roles of Activin A in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: The study identifies activin A, encoded by INHBA, as a tumor-promoting and SMAD3-dependent mechanism in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Tumor-targeted Inhba siRNA delivered with cholesterol-modified polymeric nanoparticles reduced tumor growth, metastasis, cachexia, and Ki67-positive cells while improving survival in an orthotopic mouse model, although responses varied with cellular INHBA expression.

papers.title: A set of microRNAs coordinately controls tumorigenesis, invasion, and metastasis.
papers.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
papers.summary: In pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, the miR-130a/b and miR-301a/b family was progressively up-regulated during tumorigenesis and could directly repress an Inhba/activin B 3′-UTR reporter, supporting a potential mechanism for reduced activin B signaling. The study did not functionally perturb INHBA itself, so repression of endogenous activin B and its contribution to tumor progression remain hypotheses requiring validation.

papers.title: Identification of multidrug chemoresistant genes in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells.
papers.summary: The study identifies INHBA as a gene whose knockdown partially or completely reverses chemoresistance in multiple HNSCC-derived cell models, depending on the cellular background and drug. Sirodesmin A and Carfilzomib dose-dependently reduced INHBA expression and re-sensitized cisplatin-resistant CaLH2 cells, providing experimentally supported compounds that act on the INHBA mechanism for potential repurposing, although no effects in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva were tested.

papers.title: Elevated expression of the RNA-binding protein IGF2BP1 enhances the mRNA stability of INHBA to promote the invasion and migration of esophageal squamous cancer cells.
papers.summary: This study shows that IGF2BP1 binds and stabilizes INHBA mRNA in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells, increasing INHBA protein and activating Smad2/3 signaling to promote invasion, migration, and metastasis. BTYNB disrupts the IGF2BP1–INHBA interaction and suppresses these malignant phenotypes in vitro, providing an indirect experimental strategy for targeting the INHBA mechanism.

papers.title: Inhibin beta A drives colorectal cancer progression through macrophage M2 polarization and mitochondria-dependent ferroptosis suppression.
papers.summary: The paper shows that INHBA is an oncogenic driver in colorectal cancer and that experimental INHBA knockdown suppresses tumor growth, invasion, tumor-associated macrophage M2 polarization, and mitochondrial ferroptosis. Mechanistically, INHBA stabilizes mitochondrial SLC25A10 by limiting TRIM21-mediated K48 ubiquitination, thereby activating the succinate/SUCNR1 and mtGSH/GPX4 axes; these findings support INHBA RNA silencing or direct INHBA inhibition as a transferable therapeutic concept, although no clinical intervention was tested.

papers.title: INHBA is a mediator of aggressive tumor behavior in HER2+ basal breast cancer.
papers.summary: RNA silencing and CRISPR deletion of INHBA reduced growth and invasion and increased lapatinib sensitivity in basal HER2+ breast cancer cells, while high INHBA expression was associated with poor patient outcome. The effects appeared non-canonical because Activin-receptor inhibition, follistatin, and recombinant Activin or Inhibin did not reproduce or rescue the phenotype.

papers.title: Many but not all pathogen-associated molecular patterns aggravate neurogenic heterotopic ossification after spinal cord injury.
papers.summary: The paper shows that multiple bacterial, viral, and fungal pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) exacerbate spinal-cord-injury-associated neurogenic heterotopic ossification (NHO) in mice, often through monocyte/macrophage-mediated effects on muscle fibro-adipogenic progenitor (FAP) mineralization. In human NHO-derived FAPs, Pam3CSK4, zymosan, and selected conditioned-media treatments directly or indirectly increased mineralization, while OSM and IL-1 inhibition reduced this response.

papers.title: Role of Signal Transduction Pathways and Transcription Factors in Cartilage and Joint Diseases.
papers.summary: This review describes ACVR1 gain-of-function signaling as a driver of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP), particularly through ligand-independent or activin-A-stimulated Smad1/5 signaling, chondrogenesis, and heterotopic ossification. It reports that anti-activin A antibodies, activin A inhibitors, rapamycin and other mTOR inhibitors can suppress FOP-related phenotypes in patient-derived iPSCs or mouse models, while palovarotene and REGN2477 are under clinical investigation.
papers.why: The review specifically identifies mTOR inhibitors as preventing ectopic ossification caused by ACVR1 mutations, making it directly relevant to FOP.

papers.title: When Bone Forms Where It Shouldn't: Heterotopic Ossification in Muscle Injury and Disease.
papers.summary: This review describes fibro-adipogenic progenitor cells as central mediators of heterotopic ossification and links ACVR1 (R206H) in FOP to aberrant Smad1/5/8 signalling and osteogenic FAP differentiation. It summarizes experimental interventions against inflammatory, growth-factor, neuropeptide, mechanotransduction, glucocorticoid, and calcium-regulatory pathways, but emphasizes that current heterotopic-ossification treatments have limited efficacy and substantial risks.

papers.title: Versatile role of fibro-adipogenic progenitors in neuromuscular junction homeostasis and pathology.
papers.summary: This review describes fibro-adipogenic progenitors as muscle-resident mesenchymal cells that support neuromuscular junction development, homeostasis, and regeneration through paracrine signaling, extracellular matrix modulation, and cellular interactions. It also states that aberrantly activated fibro-adipogenic progenitors promote muscle fibrosis, fatty infiltration, and ectopic bone formation, but it provides no disease-specific intervention data and does not mention ACVR1(R206H)-expressing fibro-adipogenic progenitors.

papers.title: DIPG-29. A CONNECT CONSORTIUM PRECLINICAL STUDY IDENTIFIES MEK INHIBITION AND RADIATION AS POTENTIAL COMBINATION PARTNERS FOR THE ALK2 INHIBITOR TP-0184 IN ACVR1-MUTANT DMG
papers.summary: In ACVR1-mutant diffuse midline glioma models, the ALK2 inhibitor TP-0184 inhibited BMP/SMAD signaling but showed combination-dependent activity with everolimus, trametinib, or radiation. Trametinib combinations were validated across laboratories, and TP-0184 plus radiation strongly radiosensitized three mutant models, but the cited abstract reports preclinical rather than clinical efficacy.

papers.title: DIPG-40. Combined pharmacological and genetic screening to identify dependencies and combinations in ACVR1-mutant diffuse midline glioma
papers.summary: This abstract reports that ACVR1-mutant diffuse midline glioma models are sensitive to ALK2 inhibition, with combinations of ALK2 inhibitors and PI3K/mTOR or MEK inhibitors producing reduced viability and, in prior work, extended orthotopic xenograft survival. CRISPR/Cas9 screening identified MTOR and PPP2R1A dependencies, and drug testing showed synergy between the WEE1 inhibitor AZD1775 and ALK2 inhibitors. The paper explicitly links PPP2R1A to MAPK pathway activation, but does not specifically identify p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling.

papers.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 7 in dormancy and metastasis of prostate cancer stem-like cells in bone.
papers.summary: In prostate cancer stem-like cells, bone stromal-cell-derived BMP7 activates p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling through BMPR2, increasing p21 and NDRG1 and inducing reversible senescence. BMP7 suppresses prostate cancer stem-like-cell growth and bone metastasis in vitro and in mouse models, while withdrawal restores growth and recurrence; BMPR2 knockdown attenuates these effects.

papers.title: Wnt inhibitors Dkk1 and Sost are downstream targets of BMP signaling through the type IA receptor (BMPRIA) in osteoblasts.
papers.summary: In primary mouse osteoblasts, the p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling inhibitor SB202190 blocked BMP2-induced Dkk1 expression but did not prevent Sost induction, demonstrating differential p38-dependent and Smad-dependent regulation of these Wnt inhibitors. In complementary mouse models, loss of BMPRIA reduced Dkk1 and Sost, enhanced canonical Wnt signaling, and increased bone mass, while constitutively active BMPRIA partially rescued the knockout phenotype.

papers.title: Conjugated secondary 12α-hydroxylated bile acids promote liver fibrogenesis.
papers.summary: The paper shows that conjugated secondary 12α-hydroxylated bile acids TDCA and GDCA activate hepatic stellate cells and promote liver fibrosis through TGR5-dependent ERK1/2 and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling. Inhibition of p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling with SB239063 reduced bile-acid-induced stellate-cell proliferation and fibrosis-marker expression, providing an experimentally supported intervention on the transferable pathway.

papers.title: Maintaining bovine satellite cells stemness through p38 pathway.
papers.summary: In cultured bovine satellite cells, p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling was activated during proliferation, and SB203580 preserved PAX7 expression and stemness while transiently suppressing myocyte differentiation and fusion. During long-term culture, an appropriate SB203580 concentration enhanced proliferation and retained differentiation capacity, although progressive loss of PAX7 expression and differentiation capacity still occurred.

papers.title: The HIF-1α/PLOD2 axis integrates extracellular matrix organization and cell metabolism leading to aberrant musculoskeletal repair.
papers.summary: In a burn/tenotomy mouse model of trauma-induced heterotopic ossification, the study identifies a HIF-1α/PLOD2/LOX pathway that couples glycolytic metabolism to collagen organization in mesenchymal progenitor cells. Genetic Hif1a deletion, PLOD2 inhibition, and systemic LOX inhibition reduced heterotopic ossification or osteogenic differentiation, providing mechanistically relevant targets for interruption of endochondral heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Sustained notch signaling inhibition with a gamma-secretase inhibitor prevents traumatic heterotopic ossification.
papers.summary: In a mouse burn/Achilles-tenotomy model of traumatic heterotopic ossification and in human THO lesions, sustained inhibition of Notch signaling with the gamma-secretase inhibitor DAPT reduced tendon mesenchymal progenitor-cell proliferation, chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation, and ectopic cartilage and bone formation. The findings support DAPT and related gamma-secretase inhibitors as mechanistically relevant interventions for suppressing endochondral heterotopic ossification, although specificity, longer dosing, and effects on other cell types remain unresolved.

papers.title: Pharmacological targeting of KDM6A and KDM6B, as a novel therapeutic strategy for treating craniosynostosis in Saethre-Chotzen syndrome.
papers.summary: In Twist-1del/+ mouse calvarial cells, explants, and mice, the KDM6A/KDM6B inhibitor GSK-J4 suppressed aberrant osteogenesis and reduced mineralized bone formation; local treatment also prevented premature coronal suture fusion. The paper addresses cranial intramembranous ossification rather than endochondral heterotopic ossification, so it provides a mechanistically related osteogenesis strategy but does not directly establish efficacy in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.

papers.title: Proteasome inhibition-enhanced fracture repair is associated with increased mesenchymal progenitor cells in mice.
papers.summary: In a male mouse tibial-fracture model, short-term bortezomib treatment accelerated endochondral ossification and fracture repair, increased mesenchymal progenitor-cell abundance and proliferation, and improved callus volume and biomechanical strength. These findings implicate early ubiquitin/proteasome-system activity as a therapeutic target, but young-adult fracture healing, systemic toxicity, and the lack of experiments in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva limit direct transfer to heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: Bromodomain Protein BRD4 Accelerates Glucocorticoid Dysregulation of Bone Mass and Marrow Adiposis by Modulating H3K9 and Foxp1.
papers.summary: The study identifies a BRD4-centered epigenetic pathway in which glucocorticoid excess suppresses osteogenic differentiation and promotes adipocyte formation, shifting bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells away from bone formation. The BRD4 inhibitor JQ-1 attenuates glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in cultured cells and mice, but the paper does not investigate fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva or endochondral heterotopic ossification.

papers.title: POSTN-Mediated Interplay of M1 Polarized Macrophage with Tendon-Derived Stem Cells to Drive Traumatic Heterotopic Ossification Formation through PTK7/ATK Signaling?
papers.summary: In a mouse burn/tendon-injury model, the paper shows that M1-polarized macrophages promote traumatic heterotopic ossification by secreting periostin (POSTN), which binds PTK7 in tendon-derived stem cells and increases AKT S124 phosphorylation while suppressing fatty-acid β-oxidation. Genetic or pharmacologic disruption of NF-κB, POSTN, or upstream macrophage signaling reduces heterotopic bone formation, while recombinant POSTN restores it and a POSTN inhibitor alone has no significant effect.

unread.title: Challenges in the diagnosis of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva with the ACVR1 mutation (c.774G > C, p.R258S): a case report and review of literature.
unread.why: The case provides mutation-specific molecular and clinical evidence supporting earlier diagnosis of FOP.

unread.title: Monoallelic variants in ACVR1 in a cohort of Egyptian individuals with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: The study provides a nine-patient FOP cohort, ACVR1 diagnostic testing, and genotype-phenotype associations including potentially eligible patients for palovarotene.

unread.title: Progressive Soft Tissue Swelling in a Pediatric Patient Leading to the Diagnosis of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva: A Case Report.
unread.why: The case demonstrates a concrete diagnostic pathway combining imaging, biopsy, and ACVR1 testing in a child before advanced ossification.

unread.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva. The clinical features and natural history of 34 patients.
unread.why: The cohort quantifies long-term FOP progression and identifies trauma, biopsy, surgery, injections, and dental treatment as preventable exacerbating factors.

unread.title: Acvr2b receptors transduce all BMP signaling in the zebrafish gastrula and restrict Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva ACVR1-R206H signaling in a dose-dependent manner.
unread.why: The zebrafish experiments establish ACVR2B dosage as a transferable modulator of pathogenic FOP ACVR1R206H BMP signaling.

unread.title: Hyperactive BMP and Mechanosignaling Remodel Chromatin to Drive Aberrant Osteogenesis in FOP.
unread.why: The study provides multi-omic and imaging methods and demonstrates reversible restoration of a less osteogenic chromatin state through pathway inhibition.

unread.title: The role of muscle fascia in heterotopic ossification and maintenance of skeletal muscle integrity in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: The authors develop a less tissue-disruptive model that identifies fascia and fibro-adipogenic progenitors as initiating targets of FOP ossification.

unread.title: A closed-loop cell therapy engineered to autonomously secrete Activin A inhibitor protects from fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: Engineered FOP marrow cells autonomously produced an Activin A inhibitor, trafficked to lesion-prone sites, and prevented heterotopic lesions after transplantation.

unread.title: [Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressive: a clinicopathological and molecular genetic analysis of three cases].
unread.why: Three FOP cases establish clinicopathologic, immunohistochemical, and ACVR1 sequencing criteria that can facilitate early diagnosis.

unread.title: Gut microbiome-dependent IL-1 signaling is a mediator of ACVR1R206H-driven heterotopic ossification.
unread.why: Microbiome profiling and intervention experiments identify a modifiable microbiome-IL-1 axis that suppresses spontaneous and trauma-induced FOP ossification.

unread.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in children: diagnostic pitfalls and ACVR1 genotype-phenotype spectrum.
unread.why: The ten-patient cohort validates molecular testing strategies, genotype-phenotype associations, and clinical and radiological clues for diagnosing FOP.

unread.title: Precision RNAi for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva: a combinatorial, unimolecular, allele selective approach.
unread.why: Allele-selective RNA interference, alone or combined with IL1B suppression, substantially prevented heterotopic ossification in responsive and preventative FOP mouse studies.

unread.title: Variant BMP receptor mutations causing fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) in humans show BMP ligand-independent receptor activation in zebrafish.
unread.why: The zebrafish assay functionally characterizes FOP-causing ACVR1 variants and demonstrates ligand-independent activation of BMP signaling.

unread.title: A blocking monoclonal antibody reveals dimerization of intracellular domains of ALK2 associated with genetic disorders.
unread.why: The study develops and mechanistically characterizes Rm0443 and shows that it suppresses heterotopic ossification in a human-mutant FOP mouse model.

unread.title: Morpholino-Mediated Exon Skipping Targeting Human ACVR1/ALK2 for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
unread.why: The paper describes an experimentally developed PMO exon-skipping method that reduces ACVR1 expression in FOP patient cells and supports screening of candidate antisense oligomers.

unread.title: Combined rapamycin and mesenchymal stem/stromal cells derived from induced pluripotent stem cells-mediated delivery of ACVR2B-Fc fusion protein reduces heterotopic ossification in a mouse model of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: The study demonstrates that low-dose rapamycin combined with transplanted iMSC-derived ACVR2B-Fc-producing cells reduces primary and surgery-induced heterotopic ossification in FOP mice.

unread.title: A new BMP type 1 receptor kinase inhibitor for safe and efficient oral treatment to prevent genetically induced heterotopic ossification in mice.
unread.why: RK783 suppressed BMP signaling in vitro and prevented heterotopic cartilage and bone formation in two genetic FOP mouse models after oral dosing.

unread.title: PI3Kα inhibition blocks osteochondroprogenitor specification and the hyper-inflammatory response to prevent heterotopic ossification.
unread.why: Alpelisib blocked osteochondroprogenitor specification and inflammation and prevented heterotopic ossification in experimental models relevant to FOP.

unread.title: Single-base 2'OMe-modified LNA and MOE gapmers selectively silence <i>ACVR1</i> <sup><i>R206H</i></sup> in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: Mutant-selective gapmers suppressed ACVR1 R206H RNA and protein and reduced osteogenic differentiation in patient-derived cells and engineered cells, while sparing wild-type activity.

unread.title: An inducible knock-in mouse model of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva shows spontaneous formation of heterotopic ossification.
unread.why: The inducible mouse model reproduces both injury-triggered and spontaneous FOP-type heterotopic ossification and provides a platform for testing interventions.

unread.title: Hyperactive BMP and Mechanosignaling Remodel Chromatin to Drive Aberrant Osteogenesis in FOP.
unread.why: Multi-omic and imaging experiments identified reversible FOP-specific chromatin remodeling, while Rho/ROCK and BMP-SMAD inhibition restored chromatin condensation in mutant cells.

unread.title: A closed-loop cell therapy engineered to autonomously secrete activin A inhibitor protects from fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: Engineered FOP marrow cells trafficked to lesion-prone sites, increased ActR2A-Fc in response to activin A, and reduced heterotopic lesions after transplantation in mice.

unread.title: Matrix metalloproteinase-9 deficiency confers resilience in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in a man and mice.
unread.why: The study identifies reduced MMP-9 as a resilience biomarker and shows that genetic, biologic, or pharmacologic MMP-9 inhibition abrogates heterotopic ossification in FOP models.

unread.title: Palovarotene (Sohonos), a synthetic retinoid for reducing new heterotopic ossification in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: history, present, and future.
unread.why: Reviews clinical and preclinical data showing that palovarotene reduces new heterotopic ossification in FOP while identifying important growth-plate safety risks.

unread.title: Reduced GS Domain Serine/Threonine Requirements of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva Mutant Type I BMP Receptor ACVR1 in the Zebrafish.
unread.why: Uses a zebrafish assay, structural modeling, and domain swaps to characterize how FOP ACVR1 variants activate BMP signaling.

unread.title: A Case of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva in a 5-year-old Boy with all Musculoskeletal Features and Review of the Literature.
unread.why: Provides a FOP case in which characteristic great-toe malformations and radiography enabled diagnosis and avoidance of unnecessary invasive testing.

unread.title: Palovarotene in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: review and perspective.
unread.why: Summarizes phase 2/3 evidence and regulatory use of palovarotene for inhibiting new heterotopic ossification in FOP.

unread.title: Characterization of flare-ups and impact of garetosmab in adults with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: a post hoc analysis of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled LUMINA-1 trial.
unread.why: Reports randomized-trial data showing that garetosmab reduces flare-up severity and duration and provides clinically usable flare-up and CT outcome measures.

unread.title: Effects of Renal and Hepatic Impairment on the Pharmacokinetics of Zilurgisertib.
unread.why: Provides human pharmacokinetic data for the FOP trial drug zilurgisertib that can guide dosing in patients with renal or hepatic impairment.

unread.title: Dysregulated BMP signaling and enhanced osteogenic differentiation of connective tissue progenitor cells from patients with fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).
unread.why: Establishes patient-derived connective-tissue progenitor cells as a model with ligand-independent BMP signaling, BMP hyperresponsiveness, and rapid osteogenic differentiation.

unread.title: Hematopoietic stem-cell contribution to ectopic skeletogenesis.
unread.why: Tests whether bone marrow replacement and immune suppression alter ectopic skeletogenesis, showing that transplant alone was insufficient but immunosuppression reduced skeletal ectopia.

unread.title: Variable signaling activity by FOP ACVR1 mutations.
unread.why: Directly tests FOP ACVR1 variants and shows mutation-dependent BMP/activin responsiveness and ligand-independent pathway activation.

unread.title: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva in a young adult with genetic mutation: Case report.
unread.why: This FOP case directly tested a multimodal pain-treatment regimen and intravenous bisphosphonate, with 12-month clinical follow-up, while also documenting genetic and clinical diagnostic methods.

unread.title: A case of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva associated with a novel variant of the ACVR1 gene.
unread.why: The study identifies a de novo FOP variant using genetic screening and demonstrates its aberrant receptor activity with transfection-based functional assays, providing directly reusable diagnostic and characterization methods.

unread.title: Current and emerging treatment modalities for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: The review identifies palovarotene as the first FDA-approved treatment for reducing new heterotopic ossification in FOP and summarizes its efficacy and safety limitations.

unread.title: Interplay between ALK2<sup>R206H</sup> mutant receptor and autophagy signaling regulates receptor stability and its chondrogenic functions.
unread.why: Patient-derived FOP cells and mechanistic experiments show that rapamycin and spermidine reduce ALK2 R206H-driven chondrogenic differentiation through autophagy-dependent effects.

unread.title: Discovery and Characterization of Zilurgisertib, a Potent and Selective Inhibitor of Activin Receptor-like Kinase‑2 (ALK2) for the Treatment of Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva.
unread.why: The study reports discovery and preclinical characterization of the selective ALK2 inhibitor zilurgisertib, including complete suppression of heterotopic ossification in a pediatric FOP mouse model.

unread.title: Content Validation of the Flares Diary: A Qualitative Analysis of the Flares Experience Within the Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP) Population.
unread.why: Qualitative validation in adults with FOP supports the Flares Diary as a comprehensible and clinically relevant measure of flare-up symptoms and impacts.

unread.title: Palovarotene impact on fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP): data from month 48 of the phase III MOVE trial.
unread.why: The 48-month MOVE analysis provides long-term clinical outcome and safety data for palovarotene, including effects on new heterotopic ossification and vertebral development in children.

unread.title: Efficacy and safety of garetosmab, an activin A-blocking antibody, in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (OPTIMA): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
unread.why: The randomized phase 3 OPTIMA trial shows that activin A-blocking garetosmab significantly reduces new heterotopic bone lesions versus placebo in adults with FOP.

unread.title: Activation of PPARγ redirects fibro-adipogenic progenitors to replace ectopic bone with fat in models of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and trauma-induced heterotopic ossification
unread.why: Rosiglitazone treatment eliminated ectopic bone and induced fat replacement in mouse models of FOP and trauma-induced heterotopic ossification, with corroboration from a prior human case report.

unread.title: Aberrant ciliogenesis induced by enhanced BMP signaling causes heterotopic ossification
unread.why: The study provides direct mechanistic and experimental evidence in FOP-relevant Acvr1 models that inhibiting ciliogenesis or Smoothened signaling attenuates heterotopic ossification.

unread.title: Reduction of New Heterotopic Ossification (HO) in the Open-Label, Phase 3 MOVE Trial of Palovarotene for Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva (FOP).
unread.why: The phase 3 MOVE trial reports direct clinical efficacy and safety data for palovarotene in FOP, including a validated imaging-based endpoint for new heterotopic ossification.

unread.title: Cartilage-derived retinoic acid-sensitive protein (CD-RAP): A stage-specific biomarker of heterotopic endochondral ossification (HEO) in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).
unread.why: The study directly evaluates CD-RAP as a blood biomarker of the pre-osseous stage of FOP heterotopic ossification and shows suppression by palovarotene in an FOP mouse model.

unread.title: Most Fractures Treated Nonoperatively in Individuals With Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva Heal With a Paucity of Flareups, Heterotopic Ossification, and Loss of Mobility.
unread.why: This study provides long-term evidence that nonoperative treatment of normotopic fractures in FOP usually heals without major flare-ups, heterotopic ossification, or mobility loss.

unread.title: The Pharmacokinetic Profile of Palovarotene: An Open-Label Phase I Trial Investigating the Effect of Food and Potential for Drug-Drug Interaction in Healthy Participants.
unread.why: This phase I study provides practical dosing and drug-interaction data for palovarotene, an FOP-directed treatment.

unread.title: A Pharmacokinetic, Safety, and Tolerability Trial of Palovarotene in Healthy Japanese and Non-Japanese Participants.
unread.why: This trial shows comparable palovarotene pharmacokinetics in Japanese and non-Japanese participants, supporting its use without ethnicity-based dose adjustment in FOP.

unread.title: Conversion of vascular endothelial cells into multipotent stem-like cells.
unread.why: Using human FOP lesions and ALK2-model systems, the study identifies a manipulable vascular endothelial source of osteogenic, chondrogenic, and adipogenic cells for tissue-engineering strategies.

unread.title: ACVR1R206H receptor mutation causes fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva by imparting responsiveness to activin A.
unread.why: This work establishes an accurate FOP model and demonstrates that activin-A neutralization or broad BMP blockade prevents heterotopic ossification.

unread.title: Neofunction of ACVR1 in fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva.
unread.why: The paper develops patient-derived FOP cellular models and demonstrates an assayable activin-dependent disease mechanism that can support therapeutic screening.

unread.title: Identification of progenitor cells that contribute to heterotopic skeletogenesis.
unread.why: The study identifies endothelial progenitors as contributors to every stage of heterotopic skeletogenesis, providing models and a potential cell-specific therapeutic target for FOP.
